gate:m0.text:
# #0001 — M0: the sealed schema stands
type: milestone        status: open
refs: [1] [2] [4] [9]   opened: seed   closed-by: <sha>

**Component constraint (Tier 2):** the base migrations (`0000`–`0004`) apply cleanly to a
fresh Supabase project; a direct client INSERT into any application table is denied at the
grant layer; a granted SECURITY DEFINER function writes, stamps ownership from `auth.uid()`,
and records to `audit_log`.
**Traces to (Tier 1):** "auditing write security is reading the function list" — the seal is
the product.

Exit tests:
- `test_m0_grants`: as `authenticated`, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every app table → permission denied.
- `test_m0_definer`: example function writes a row owned by the caller; `audit_log` gains one entry.
- `test_m0_identity`: no client-granted function signature contains a user-id parameter (lint over pg_proc).
gate:m0.title: M0: the sealed schema stands

gate:m1.text:
# #0002 — M1: the four gates hold
type: milestone        status: open
refs: [5] [6] [7] [m0]   opened: seed   closed-by: <sha>
deps: defers-to #0004; informs #0003

**Component constraint (Tier 2):** the access-token hook stamps `user_role` and
`dpa_version` into the JWT; `assert_consent()` blocks a caller whose accepted version is
stale; `assert_assurance()` refuses `aal1` and refuses `aal2` older than
`app_settings.mfa_max_age`, and passes a fresh challenge.
**Traces to (Tier 1):** long-lived reading sessions, fresh 2FA exactly where writing is
sensitive.

`defers-to #0004` — the flat role model ships now; the flat-vs-permission decision (Q1) is
deliberately open and this milestone takes the conservative (flat) reading.
`informs #0003` — the gate predicates are what the shell's route guards mirror.

Exit tests:
- `test_m1_hook`: fresh token for a seeded user carries both claims.
- `test_m1_consent`: bump `legal_documents` version → gated function refuses until re-accept.
- `test_m1_assurance`: elevated function refuses stale MFA, passes within window; window read from settings.
gate:m1.title: M1: the four gates hold

gate:m2.text:
# #0003 — M2: the shell pumps one slice end-to-end
type: milestone        status: open
refs: [10] [S3] [m1]   opened: seed   closed-by: <sha>

**Component constraint (Tier 2):** the SvelteKit skeleton (ssr=false) serves login, 2FA
enrol/challenge, and the consent gate; the island mount honours `init(el)/destroy()` across
client-side navigation; one example slice (spec → migration from templates → island page) is
generated by an agent session and passes review against its spec.
**Traces to (Tier 1):** "pumped out fast" — the base is proven the day one feature costs one
spec plus one session.

Freezing seam S3 (the mount contract) is requested when this latches — the first scheduled
substitute renderer is OCreate.

Exit tests:
- `test_m2_navigation`: island `destroy()` fires on route change; no document-level handler leaks.
- `test_m2_slice`: the example slice's migration applies; its function passes the M0/M1 test shapes.
gate:m2.title: M2: the shell pumps one slice end-to-end

hold:rate-limit-placement.text:
# #0005 — Ambiguity: rate-limit placement (in-DB vs edge)
type: ambiguity        status: open
refs: [8] [S2]   opened: seed   closed-by: <human sign-off>
deps: informs #0006

**The open decision:** constraint 8 mandates the *analysis* per client-granted function;
implementation is deferred by decision. When implemented: an in-DB `rate_limits` table keeps
the "function body is the entire policy" property but spends DB cycles; an edge tier keeps the
DB pure but reopens a server dependency for hot functions.
**Traces to (Tier 1):** every open door has a named cost — where the meter lives is the open
half of that promise.

Until closed, `rate_note()` (a documented no-op) carries each function's analysis in-schema.
Resolution lands behind seam S2 in Phase B.
hold:rate-limit-placement.title: Ambiguity: rate-limit placement (in-DB vs edge)

hold:roles-model.text:
# #0004 — Ambiguity: flat roles vs role→permission indirection
type: ambiguity        status: open
refs: [5] [S1]   opened: seed   closed-by: <human sign-off>
deps: informs #0002

**The open decision:** constraint 5 fixes *where* authorization is read (JWT claims); it does
not fix the role vocabulary's shape. Flat (`user_roles`, one claim) ships now. Whether apps
built on this base will diverge enough in vocabulary to warrant `has_permission()` indirection
is undecided — choosing silently in code would be accidental design.
**Traces to (Tier 1):** "one mechanism serves everything" — the wrong shape here multiplies
into every function body.

The code takes the conservative reading (flat) until a human closes this; the upgrade path is
seam S1 (migration touching only `0001_roles.sql` and the token hook).
hold:roles-model.title: Ambiguity: flat roles vs role→permission indirection
